# Mutants argued equivalent or unreachable, one line per mutant: file | function |
# description | #PR, the pull request whose body gives the argument.
# The mutants workflow's summary lists as "New misses" only the missed and timed-out
# mutants this list doesn't account for (.github/workflows/mutants.yml); it never changes
# which mutants are tested.
#
# The key is cargo-mutants' name without its line and column, which move: the file, the
# function after the last " in " (for a whole function replaced, the function it names;
# outside a function, empty), and the description before it. Mutants with one key are told
# apart only by how many there are: a key missed more times than it's listed here is new,
# and all its misses are listed. Add a mutant with the PR that argues it; remove its line
# when a test kills it or its code goes.

# A release (`drag_end`) runs as a queued command, so a session's close while it runs
# closes its ticket: `close` either finds the command recorded and closes it, or the
# command, recorded after `close` ended the queue, finds the session closed and closes its
# own ticket. The release registers its stop with that ticket before it moves or solves
# (at once stopped, if the ticket is closed already) and keeps it until both are done, and
# that stop is the very `DragStop` `stop_release` stops: with it gone, the close still
# stops the release's move and solve, at the same point.

# The sketch tools (#335). `to_segment`'s `span > 0.0`: a span of 0 is a line of no length,

# point before it looks at curves, so the foot is never read. `tangent_arc`'s `s > 0.0`: `s` is
# 0 only where |d|² underflows (|d| under about 1.5e-162, with a tolerance of 0), which only
# a preview can meet; an add needs its end more than 1e-7 from its start. `counter_clockwise`'s
# `< 0.0`: its cross product is `circumcentre`'s, which returns none for 0 before
# `counter_clockwise` is asked. The tool's tolerance, `context.tolerance > 0.0`: at 0 either
# side gives 0 (or −0, which every comparison takes as 0). `turn`'s inner `+ PI` as `− PI`:
# the two differ by a whole turn, which `rem_euclid` takes away, so only in rounding, and
# both give −π at ±π.

# take SD4's path first), so never 0. `lines`' `cross(ray_a, ray_b) > 0.0`: each ray is its
# line's direction or its negation, so that cross is ± the lines' cross, exactly, never 0 for

# The viewport's zoom stop (#341). `View::zoom` caps an orthographic zoom in at `most`, the
# octaves down to `least`, the least view height the drawn bodies' reach allows in the pane
# (`views::least_view_height(rows, reach)`, rows × reach / 2^19 × 1.01, the pane's rows at
# least 1): `reach` is a max over finite boxes from a finite target, so `least` is finite
# and never below 0 (0 for no box), and
# the camera's view height is positive and finite. `scroll > 0.0` as `>= 0.0`: at a scroll of
# 0 (or −0) the cap gives 0 (or −0) again, and `scroll != 0.0` zooms by neither. `least > 0.0`
# as `>= 0.0`: at a least of 0, `most` is −200 · log2(0) = +∞, which caps nothing. `&&` as
# `||`: a zoom out (scroll ≤ 0) is never above the cap, which is at least 0, so `min` keeps
# it; a zoom in with a least of 0 is capped at +∞, as above. Each gives the scroll unchanged.
crates/silico-app/src/viewport.rs | View::zoom | replace > with >= | #341
crates/silico-app/src/viewport.rs | View::zoom | replace > with >= | #341
crates/silico-app/src/viewport.rs | View::zoom | replace && with || | #341
# The core's fit (#341). `fit_along` takes the extents of a box's eight corners along `up`
# and the image's right as the least and most of their dot products. Each corner's
# coordinate on one axis is chosen by one bit of `i`, `low` for 0 and `high` for 1:
# `i & 1 == 0` as `!= 0` (or bit 2's, or bit 4's) swaps `low` and `high` on that axis for
# every `i`, so the loop meets the same eight corners in another order, and a least and a
# most over a set don't depend on its order.
crates/silico-core/src/views.rs | fit_along | replace == with != | #341
crates/silico-core/src/views.rs | fit_along | replace == with != | #341

# The frame's left and right events numbered together (#371). `sequenced` puts a right click
# first when its place is less than the next left event's: `r < l` as `r <= l` differs only
# for a right click and a left event of one place. A place is 0 (a Cancel a navigation tool
# forces: a left event) or i + 1 for the frame's i-th egui event, and one egui event is one
# button's: a PointerButton event makes a left event or a right click, never both, and
# WindowFocused(false) makes a left Cancel and only ends a right press, making no click. So
# no two of one place come from both lists, and either comparison gives the same order.

# The edges' cut (#353). `View::cut_strip` builds a strip from each segment's kept part: it
# pushes the part's start and end (two points) when a strip begins, and one more point for
# each segment that carries it on, and takes the strip away (leaving it empty) whenever it's
# ended. So at the top of each segment the strip holds no point or at least two, never one:
# `strip.len() > 1` as `>= 1` in the branch of a segment wholly outside ends the same strips.
# And `leave < 1.0` as `leave > 1.0` (never so: `leave` is at most 1) never ends a strip
# where a segment leaves the pyramid; the strip is ended all the same where it would be next,
# with nothing pushed between: the next segment starts at that end, outside the half-space
# it left by (its form there below 0), so the next segment is wholly outside (the branch
# above ends the strip), or enters at a fraction above 0 (`fa / (fa - fb)` with `fa` below 0
# and `fb` at least 0), which ends it before it begins another; or there's no next segment,
# and the strip is ended after the loop. Each gives the same strips.
crates/silico-render/src/render.rs | View::cut_strip | replace > with >= | #353
crates/silico-render/src/render.rs | View::cut_strip | replace < with > | #353

# Sketch mode's drawing (#351). `aside`: `normal` is (−y, x) of a segment longer than
# nothing (a zero one is returned straight down first) divided by that length, so its x and
# y are never both 0; `normal.x <= 0.0` beside `normal.y == 0.0` differs from `<` only at
# x = 0, which with y = 0 is that zero normal. `segments`: past `radius <= tolerance ||
# sweep <= 0.0` (which returns 1), both finite and the tolerance above 0, the quotient
# tolerance/radius is in (0, 1), so 1 − it is in (0, 1] and `step`, twice its acos, in
# [0, π): finite, so `step <= 0.0 && !step.is_finite()` is never true, and the guard is
# true only at a step of 0 (a radius so far past the tolerance that 1 − the quotient rounds
# to 1), where the sweep, above 0, over it is infinite, at least the cap: the cap either way.
crates/silico-app/src/sketch/draw.rs | aside | replace < with <= | #351
crates/silico-app/src/sketch/draw.rs | segments | replace || with && | #351
# Sketch mode's hit-testing (#351): a tolerance that's no number or below 0 finds nothing
# either way. Every distance `hit` compares with it is a length (a point's, a box's, a
